To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the brain activity patterns for basic emotions can be reliably decoded from fMRI data using machine learning techniques.
the brain has specific signatures of emotions that can be used to classify the emotional state of an individual from fMRI data.

(1) brain activity patterns are distinct for different emotions, and (2) the patterns are consistent across induction methods (i.e., movies and mental imagery), across individuals, and across brain imaging techniques (i.e., fMRI and MEG).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neural basis of human emotion.
the question how the brain represents emotional states, and how these representations are related to the emotional experiences.
the study of emotions, and more specifically with the study of how emotions are represented in the brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the neural signatures of basic emotions are discrete.

the brain represents emotions as discrete patterns of activation in a set of brain regions that are not necessarily the same as the brain regions that are responsible for the generation of the emotional response.
the brain regions that are most active in the experience of basic emotions are those that are most involved in the processing and integration of sensory and cognitive information.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the brain has discrete representations of the 6 basic emotions that are independent of the induction method, that these representations generalize across individuals, and that the representations are associated with the subjective experience.
the brain represents basic emotions in a distributed fashion, and that these representations are not only categorical, but also graded and continuous.
the human brain represents basic emotions as discrete, multimodal patterns of neural activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the neural representation of emotions is categorical and that it is independent of the method of induction.
there is no evidence for distinct neural patterns of basic emotions.
basic emotions have discrete neural signatures that can be decoded from brain activity.
